answer: For standard retail claims, the main reimbursement claim must be submitted within 30 days from the date of discharge [2]. For group corporate plans, the submission window is 60 days from discharge [3]. (Under archived 2024 rules, the deadline was 15 days from the date of discharge [1].)
Under the Aurora Silver plan, the room rent limit is 2% of the sum insured per day [3].
No, maternity is not covered on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1][2].

The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months on retail plans and the Aurora Hospital Cash Benefit plan [2][4][5]. However, for the Aurora Senior Care plan, the waiting period is 24 months [2]. Waiting periods already served with a previous Indian insurer can carry over upon portability up to the previous policy's sum insured [3].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1][2].
As of 1 April 2026, Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns [1].

The no-claim bonus on the Aurora Gold plan is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating to a maximum of 100% [1][4]. If a claim is made, the accumulated bonus is not reduced, but it stops accumulating for that year only [1].
No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment [1]. IVF, infertility, assisted reproduction, surrogacy, and sterilisation reversal are listed under permanent treatment-related exclusions [1].
The cataract surgery sub-limit on the Gold plan is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If you are not satisfied with the initial response from customer service, you can escalate the matter to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer (GRO) [1]. If Aurora's final response is unsatisfactory, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [3]. Additionally, you retain the right to escalate the dispute to a consumer forum or civil court [3].

Ambulance cover is ₹5,000 per hospitalisation for road ambulance only, which applies across all plans [1]. Specific plan terms for both the Silver and Bronze tiers confirm an ambulance sub-limit of ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [3][5].
Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness [1]. The standard 30-day initial waiting period applies, with no separate waiting period required [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned or cancelled for a refund [2][5]. It lasts 15 days from receiving the policy document, or 30 days for policies sold through distance marketing, and allows the policyholder to receive a premium refund minus proportionate risk premium, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [1][2].
You earn 150 wellness points per year for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advances, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [2]. Out-patient treatment is not considered a day-care procedure [2].
For an emergency admission under the cashless route, the hospital must notify Aurora within 24 hours of admission [1].
No, Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a Third Party Administrator (TPA) [1].
To qualify as a hospital under the policy, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or at least 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].

No, not everything will be paid because taking a room at ₹15,000 per day exceeds your Silver room-rent limit of 2% (₹10,000 per day on a ₹5,00,000 sum insured) [1][2]. Because of proportionate deduction, Aurora will reduce the room charges and all associated medical expenses—such as surgeon, anaesthetist, OT, and nursing fees—in the ratio of 10,000 to 15,000, requiring you to pay the difference out of pocket [1][2]. Only pharmacy and consumables are not subject to proportionate reduction [1].
